name: birta
description: A shared workspace for teams working with different AI agents. Keep documents and the context behind them together, so anyone on the team can pick up the work with their agent of choice. Every project adds to your team's shared knowledge: source material, discussions, decisions and revisions. Review reports, decks, proposals and interactive pages together, leave comments where changes are needed, and ask your agent to revise them.

capabilities: Work on the same projects from different AI agents
Keep source material, discussions and decisions with each document
Pick up a teammate's work with your own connected agent
Create reports, decks, proposals and interactive pages
Use skills for document structure, design and clear writing
Share work with teammates and clients for review
Leave comments on specific page elements and Markdown blocks
Ask your agent to apply feedback and publish the next version
Keep version history and restore earlier work
Collect form submissions, track visits and connect a custom domain
defaultPrompt: Turn these notes into a report in Birta and share it with my team for review.
Open our team's Birta project, read the discussion and continue the proposal from the latest version.
Read the comments on our Birta page, make the changes and publish the next version.
interface.longDescription:
Birta is a shared workspace for teams working with different AI agents. Each person connects the agent they prefer, and everyone works with the same projects, files, versions and discussions. Nobody has to switch tools to join the work.

Every project adds to your team's shared knowledge: source material, discussions, decisions and revisions stay next to the result. The next person and their agent can see what was decided and continue from there, without asking the author to explain it all again.

Create reports, presentations, proposals, documentation, landing pages, portfolios, event pages, prototypes and small interactive tools. Built-in skills guide structure, design and clear writing, so work from different agents follows the same standards. Birta supports HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images and Markdown, so the result opens in a browser.

Share a link with your team or a client. When link access is enabled, they can open it without an account and leave comments on specific elements or Markdown blocks. You can also restrict access to project members.

Ask your agent to read the comments, revise the work, reply in each thread and publish the next version. Each project keeps its address across updates, and published versions remain available to restore.

Add forms, manage incoming requests, check visitor statistics and connect a custom domain when a page needs to do more.

For teams and specialists who use agents every day and share their work with teammates, managers or clients.

Birta hosts static sites and Markdown documents. It does not run server-side application code or serve PDFs as pages. Access and form submissions follow project settings and account limits.

publication.release_notes: Birta skills come to the app. Base skills: birta-setup connects Birta and asks for the first goal, birta-publish takes work to a published version and through feedback, birta-manage handles access, people, lead forms, domains and stats, plus writing, page design, diagrams, charts and binary files. Skills for a kind of work: presentation, report, proposal, landing page, portfolio, event, spec, guide and tool. Mention the agent by name in a review thread and ChatGPT can receive the mention as an event. Images, fonts and other binary files go into a draft with one HTTP send to an upload address. Projects carry tags: the project list shows them and filters by them, and a project's tags can be set when it is created or replaced later. The listing now describes Birta as a shared workspace for teams on different AI agents.

positive.description: Create a page and publish it. Starts from an empty account; later cases use the project it creates.
positive.prompt: Make a one-page report on global coffee consumption and publish it with Birta.
positive.expected_behavior: A new project is created, the report is written to it and version 1 is published. The reply gives two links: the live site address, where the report opens without an account, and a review link for that version.

positive.description: Revise published work by asking. Runs after the first case.
positive.prompt: Change the headline to 'Coffee in 2026' and publish the update.
positive.expected_behavior: The live site address now shows the headline Coffee in 2026 as version 2, and the project in the Birta dashboard lists both versions.

positive.description: Act on review remarks. Runs after the second case. Before running, open the review link of the latest version in a browser, click a block on the page and leave a remark, for example: add a one-line takeaway under the headline.
positive.prompt: Read the remarks, make the changes, and publish the update.
positive.tools_triggered: list_projects, list_versions, list_version_comments, create_version, read_file, edit_file, reply_to_thread, publish_version
positive.expected_behavior: The reply names the remark and says it was applied; the change the reviewer asked for is on the page at the same address as version 3, and the remark's thread gets a reply describing the change.

positive.description: Change who can open a project. Runs after the first case: a new project opens only for its owner and invited people.
positive.prompt: Let anyone with the link open my Birta coffee consumption report, then tell me who can open it now.
positive.expected_behavior: Project access changes to anyone with the link; the reply says so, and the site address now opens in a signed-out browser.

positive.description: Collect requests with a form. Runs after the fourth case, so the form can be filled in a signed-out browser.
positive.prompt: Add a feedback form to my Birta coffee consumption report, publish it, and after I send a test request, show me the requests it received.
positive.tools_triggered: list_projects, list_versions, create_form, create_version, read_file, edit_file, publish_version, list_leads
positive.expected_behavior: The published page shows a feedback form; after the reviewer submits it, the reply lists that request with the name and message entered.

negative.description: A request unrelated to documents, pages or Birta projects: the plugin should not act and no Birta tool is called.
negative.prompt: What will the weather be in Paris tomorrow?

negative.description: Birta hosts static sites and Markdown documents only: the agent should explain it cannot run server code or a database there, and publish nothing.
negative.prompt: Deploy my Node.js Express API with its Postgres database to Birta.

negative.description: No tool deletes a project: the agent should say projects are deleted from the Birta dashboard and change nothing.
negative.prompt: Delete all of my Birta projects.
